issues.description: The problem statement explicitly instructs students to call setup_env() with no parameters (problem_statement.md lines 21-22). The solution, however, declares extern setup_env and invokes it after pushing a value (push 1; call setup_env), implying it expects one argument (solution_repository/helloWorld.asm lines 8,13-14). The template does not declare or reference setup_env at all (template_repository/helloWorld.asm lines 1-19). This mismatch (no-parameter vs. one-parameter usage, and missing declaration in the template) can confuse students about the correct calling convention for setup_env and whether they must add an extern declaration or push an argument. It could lead to incorrect student solutions or failing tests if the intended signature differs.
issues.suggested_fix:
Make the intended signature and usage of setup_env consistent across artifacts. Options:
1) If setup_env takes no parameters (as the problem text states): remove the push 1 from the solution and call setup_env with no arguments; add an extern setup_env declaration to the template (and optionally a TODO comment) so students know to call it. 
2) If setup_env is intended to take one parameter: update the problem statement to document the required parameter(s) and calling convention, and add an extern setup_env declaration to the template so students can call it correctly. Ensure the solution and template match the documented signature.
